groups.label: Education and Soul Order
groups.summary: Socrates establishes that musical simplicity and steadfast nurture protect civil character, while psychological distinctions rest on the formal principle of non-contradiction.
groups.rationale: These early foundational discussions in Books III and IV link cultural discipline and musical training to the structural harmony and consistency of the soul.

groups.label: Philosophy and the Highest Good
groups.summary: Socrates outlines the nature of true philosophers as lovers of immutable truth, defining faculties by their operation, ideals as normative measures, and the idea of the good as supreme knowledge.
groups.rationale: A contiguous sequence from Books V and VI defining the epistemological standards, cognitive powers, and ultimate metaphysical object governing the philosopher.

groups.label: Forms, Reason, and Dialectic
groups.summary: Socrates warns against premature exposure to dialectic, identifies divine reason or external law as the necessary governor of human character, and illustrates the degrees of reality through the three beds.
groups.rationale: These passages examine how humans engage metaphysical truth and divine order, from training in dialectic and internal rational governance to ontological hierarchies.

groups.label: Degenerate Regimes and Souls
groups.summary: Socrates details the progressive decline of civic constitutions and individual souls through timocracy, oligarchy, democratic license, factional class divisions, and despotic tyranny.
groups.rationale: A unified sequence in Book VIII examining the systematic degeneration of character and state forms under spiraling appetites and passions.

groups.label: Tyranny and Final Retribution
groups.summary: Socrates calculates the 729-fold misery separating the tyrant from the king and recounts Er's vision of posthumous rewards, tenfold penalties, and the eternal torment of tyrants.
groups.rationale: Both passages demonstrate the profound consequences of vice and tyranny, evaluating their wretchedness in mathematical measure and eschatological judgement.
